unit.why: A single anecdote about the pre-Hasidic kabbalist R. Shimshon of Ostropol testing R. Heschel (of Kraków), passed down through family transmission.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי משארינו הג׳ המנוח מוה׳ יוסף שאול
stories.summary_en: It was revealed to the kabbalist R. Shimshon of Ostropol that he would share R. Heschel's portion in Paradise, so he disguised himself as a sick stranger to test him; R. Heschel bore it patiently, and at night Shimshon heard his weeping and trembling at Tikkun Hatzot and then revealed himself.

tags.why: Praises pre-Hasidic rabbinic and kabbalist figures (R. Heschel, R. Shimshon of Ostropol)

quotes: להמקובל ר״ש מאוסטריפאלי נתגלה שיהיה חלקו בחד
tags.why: His shared portion in Gan Eden is disclosed to him

quotes: שיהיה חלקו בחד עם זקינינו הרב ר׳ העשיל בג״ע
tags.why: Concerns their portion in the world to come
He uses a disguise to deceive R. Heschel

quotes: גודל הבכיות ורעידת עצמותיו בתיקון החצות
tags.why: R. Heschel's bones tremble during his midnight devotion
Tikkun Hatzot (the midnight lament) is depicted
R. Heschel's forbearance and hospitality toward the stranger
The tale illustrates R. Heschel's patience and piety
The stranger turns out to be the kabbalist
